subject: math
topicName: Geometry - Lesson 8: Converse of Pythagorean Theorem
description: Classify triangles as right, acute, or obtuse by comparing the square of the longest side with the sum of the squares of the two shorter sides.
learningObjectives: Order triangle side lengths and identify the longest side as c
Use the converse of the Pythagorean Theorem to test whether a triangle is right
Compare a^2 + b^2 with c^2 to classify triangles as right, acute, or obtuse
Decide when side lengths do not form a triangle before attempting classification
Avoid the common error of choosing c before sorting the side lengths
prerequisites: Find squares of whole numbers and decimals
Use the Pythagorean Theorem for right triangles
